assertion_analysis.fails_when: Restoring inline admission selection produces no cached selector call (observed 0 versus required 1 in reuse-negative-control.log); repeated delegation also fails the exact count.
Passing a new list, filtered copy or reread rather than the same held all_records object fails identity; the assertion checks cache sharing rather than only selected content.
Selecting no design, a content review or a wrong stored review fails the fixed review-design fixture identity.
Removing numeric ordering picks version 2 instead of version 10, or failing rubric filtering picks the content record at version 999.

Removing cached plan filtering picks the other plan at version 1000; removing rubric filtering picks content at 999; lexical ordering picks 2; ignoring the iterator is additionally caught by the final store-read assertion.
Treating an explicit empty cache as missing and falling back to the store returns a review rather than None.
Any store read by either cached call adds entries beyond the single expected default read; suppressing the default read also fails.

assertion_independence: The selected newest object is also an input candidate, but the expected choice is fixed by plan, rubric and numeric version and competing decoys make these identity checks fail under selection regressions; none is a self-comparison that survives the claimed regression.
